By parts with 1 as second function: \(\int (\log x)^2 \cdot 1\,dx = x(\log x)^2 - \int 2\log x \cdot \frac{1}{x} \cdot x\,dx = x(\log x)^2 - 2\int \log x\,dx = x(\log x)^2 - 2[x\log x - \int dx] = x(\log x)^2 - 2x\log x + 2x + C\).

\(\tan^{-1} x = \frac{1}{a}\log y \Rightarrow a\tan^{-1} x = \log y\); differentiate: \(\frac{a}{1 + x^2} = \frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}\), so \((1 + x^2)\frac{dy}{dx} = ay\). Differentiate again: \((1 + x^2)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2x\frac{dy}{dx} = a\frac{dy}{dx}\), giving the result. Alternative: \(\frac{dx}{dy} = \sec^2\left(\frac{1}{a}\log y\right) \cdot \frac{1}{ay}\) so \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{ay}{1 + x^2}\), then as above.

Using \(\int_a^b f(x)dx = \int_a^b f(a + b - x)dx\): \(I = \int_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4} \frac{\pi - x}{1 + \sin x}dx\), so \(2I = \pi\int_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4} \frac{dx}{1 + \sin x} = \pi\int \frac{1 - \sin x}{\cos^2 x}dx = \pi\int (\sec^2 x - \sec x\tan x)dx = \pi[\tan x - \sec x]_{\pi/4}^{3\pi/4}\), giving \(I = \frac{\pi}{2}[-1 - (-\sqrt{2}) - 1 + \sqrt{2}] = \frac{\pi}{2}(2\sqrt{2} - 2) = \pi(\sqrt{2} - 1)\). Alternatives: write \(1 + \sin x = 2\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{x}{2}\right)\) and integrate \(\frac{1}{2}x\sec^2\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{x}{2}\right)\) by parts; or multiply by \(1 - \sin x\) and integrate \(x\sec^2 x - x\tan x\sec x\) by parts.
